# A single Visium slice with H&E

!!! tip "Starting from the platform's own files"
    `staig.run("path/to/outs")` reads Space Ranger, Visium HD, Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMx, Stereo-seq,
    Slide-seq and seqFISH outputs directly; see [Input formats](input_formats.md). This page uses the
    paper's DLPFC slice.

Install STAIG with `[image]` for fresh image extraction. `STAIG_DATA` should point
to the unpacked `Dataset` directory itself, containing `DLPFC/`, `other/` and
`v10x/`. Passing `root=` overrides the environment variable. With neither set,
the default is `./Dataset`.

```python
import os
import staig
from staig import datasets, img, metrics, pl

adata = datasets.load_dlpfc(
    "151673", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True,
)
print(adata.shape, adata.obsm["spatial"].shape)
```

`download=True` downloads a missing slice folder from
[Zenodo record 14231773](https://zenodo.org/records/14231773). An existing folder
is loaded directly; if it is incomplete, call `datasets.download_dataset` with
`members=["DLPFC/151673"]` explicitly. Labels are aligned to barcodes and
unlabelled spots are dropped by default, matching the released embeddings.

## Use the released histology features

The loader attaches `embeddings.npy` to `obsm["image_features"]`. Passing the
array through the image API demonstrates the same interface used for externally
computed features. It does not retrain BYOL.

```python
img.extract_image_features(adata, method=adata.obsm["image_features"].copy())
model = staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7)
pl.spatial(adata, color=["ground_truth", "staig_domain"])
scores = metrics.evaluate(adata)
print(scores)
```

`run` preprocesses expression, constructs the graph, trains, embeds and clusters.
It returns a fitted `STAIG` model and writes results into `adata`. The default
configuration uses 400 epochs; for a short CPU check, replace the training line
with `staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, epochs=30, device="cpu", verbose=False)`.
`preset="auto"` selects a configuration from the data. `image="auto"` can
extract BYOL features when a full-resolution image is discoverable and features
are absent; use `image=None` to skip automatic extraction. The loader-supplied
features in this example are reused. Default single-slice clustering uses Python
GMM and spatial refinement. Evaluation
stores ARI/NMI (where labels exist), silhouette coefficient (SC) and
Davies–Bouldin index (DB).

## Extract features from the full-resolution image

This is an alternative starting from a fresh AnnData object. It needs the full
H&E image, image extras and ImageNet weights (downloaded by torchvision on first
use). It is substantially more expensive than loading the released embeddings.

```python
fresh = datasets.load_dlpfc(
    "151673", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True, image_features=None,
)
img.extract_image_features(
    fresh, method="byol", epochs=1, batch_size=16,
    num_workers=0, n_jobs=1, cache_dir=".cache/151673-byol-default",
)
fresh_model = staig.run(fresh, n_clusters=7)
```

The loader records the source folder, so the image extractor can find
`spatial/tissue_full_image.tif`. For your own folder, pass `image=` explicitly
if lookup fails. See the [histology tutorial](tutorials/visium_with_histology.md)
for coordinate conventions and cache rules.

## AnnData keys

These are the keys the pipeline writes (see `docs/dev/DESIGN.md`). Entries are
created only when the corresponding step runs.

| Key | Written by | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `obsm["spatial"]` | User / dataset loader | Full-resolution `(x, y)` pixel coordinates for Visium; platform coordinates otherwise |
| `obs[batch_key]` | `pp.concat_slices` | Categorical slice identifier for integration |
| `obs["ground_truth"]` | `pp.load_labels` / loader | Optional labels; unlabelled spots dropped by default |
| `obsm["X_staig_input"]` | `pp.preprocess` / `pp.concat_slices` | Dense float32 matrix of model input features |
| `obsm["image_features"]` | `img.extract_image_features` / loader | Raw features, typically 2048 dimensions for ResNet-50/BYOL; custom dimensions allowed |
| `obsm["image_pcs"]` | `graph.image_pcs`, called by model preparation | Standardised/PCA image features; default 16 PCs |
| `obsp["spatial_connectivities"]` | `graph.spatial_neighbors` | Symmetric binary CSR graph, no self-loops; block-diagonal across slices |
| `obsp["staig_edge_prob"]` | `graph.edge_removal_probabilities` | Directed CSR edge-removal probabilities; row-normalised in image/gene modes when nonzero weights exist; constant in fixed mode |
| `obs["staig_pseudo_label"]` | `graph.pseudo_labels` | Image-PC k-means labels when pseudo-label debiasing is active |
| `obsm["X_staig"]` | `STAIG.embed`, also called by `fit` | Float32 embedding, 64 dimensions by default |
| `obs["staig_domain"]` | `cluster.cluster`, also called by `run` | Categorical domain labels, refined when requested |
| `uns["staig"]` | Pipeline stages / `metrics.evaluate` | Source, preprocessing, graph, image metadata, config, resolved negative count, training history/timings, optional consensus metadata and evaluated metrics |

The image extractor stores raw features; PCA occurs during model preparation
unless you call `graph.image_pcs` yourself. This revision does not automatically
record dependency versions in `uns["staig"]`. Most preprocessing/graph functions
mutate in place and return `None` unless `copy=True`; `run` returns a model, and
`embed` returns an array. There is no `staig.tl` namespace in this revision.


---

<!-- Source: docs/input_formats.md -->

# Input formats: start from what your platform writes

Most users do not have an `.h5ad`; they have the output folder of the instrument software. `staig.read`
recognises those folders and files, builds the AnnData STAIG needs (raw counts, coordinates, metadata,
control features removed, low-count cells removed) and records what it did in `uns["staig"]`.
`staig.run` accepts the same paths directly, so the whole analysis is

```python
import staig
model = staig.run("path/to/spaceranger_outs")        # any supported layout, see the table below
adata = model.adata                                   # obs["staig_domain"], obsm["X_staig"], uns["staig"]
```

or, on the command line,

```bash
staig inspect path/to/outs                            # what would be read: platform, cells, genes, QC
staig run path/to/outs --output domains.h5ad          # read -> preprocess -> train -> cluster
staig run slide_a/ slide_b/ --output integrated.h5ad  # several inputs = alignment-free integration
```

The GUI (`staig gui`) has the same platform selector. Nothing has to be converted by hand.

## Supported layouts

| platform | what `staig.read` looks for | coordinates | removed by default | preset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10x Visium (Space Ranger 1.x–4.x) | the run folder or its `outs/`, or any folder with `*filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` (or the MTX folder) and `spatial/` (`tissue_positions.csv` or `tissue_positions_list.csv`, `scalefactors_json.json`, images); optional `truth.txt`, `embeddings.npy`; `load_images=False` keeps coordinates and scale factors | full-resolution pixels | non-gene features (e.g. Antibody Capture; counted in `obs["control_counts"]`), spots without a position | `visium` / `visium_no_image` |
| 10x Visium HD (Space Ranger 3.x/4.x) | the run folder or its `outs/` with `binned_outputs/square_XXXum/` (`bin_size=8` µm by default), one bin folder or its `.h5`; `level="cells"` reads `segmented_outputs/filtered_feature_cell_matrix.h5` with cell positions from `barcode_mappings.parquet` + 2 µm bins (mean bin position) or, failing that, the area centroid of the segmentation polygon | full-resolution pixels (`microns_per_pixel` recorded) | bins with `in_tissue == 0`, empty bins | `visium_hd` (= `stereo_seq`) |
| 10x Xenium (XOA 1.x–4.x, Xenium Ranger) | `outs/` with `cell_feature_matrix.h5` (or the MTX folder), `cells.parquet` / `cells.csv.gz`, `experiment.xenium` | microns (`x_centroid`, `y_centroid`) | Negative Control Probe/Codeword, Unassigned/Deprecated Codeword, Genomic Control features; cells < 10 transcripts | `xenium` (= `merfish`) |
| Vizgen MERSCOPE | `*cell_by_gene.csv` + `*cell_metadata.csv` (`EntityID`/`cell` ids; `center_x`, `center_y`, `fov`, `volume`) | microns | `Blank-*` barcodes; cells < 20 counts | `merscope` (= `merfish`) |
| Bruker/NanoString CosMx SMI (AtoMx flat files) | `*exprMat_file.csv[.gz]` + `*metadata_file.csv[.gz]` (one slide per folder; cells keyed `fov_cell_ID` or the `cell` column) | whole-slide pixels (`CenterX/Y_global_px`; `coordinates="local"` for per-FOV pixels) | `NegPrb*`, `Negative*`, `SystemControl*`, `FalseCode*` probes; `cell_ID == 0` (background); cells < 20 counts | `cosmx` (= `merfish`) |
| BGI Stereo-seq (SAW) | `.gef` (square-bin or cell-bin HDF5 after the SAW file-format manual, `offset` tables honoured), `.gem` / `.gem.gz` / `.tsv` with `geneID x y MIDCount [ExonCount] [CellID]` (`MIDCounts`, `UMICount`, `label` accepted; `#` header lines kept in `uns["staig"]["gem_header"]`). Bins are formed on the absolute grid `floor(coordinate / bin_size)` (stored coordinate = bin centre), read in 4-million-row chunks | DNB indices (1 DNB = 0.5 µm) | background labels `0`/`-1`, bins/cells < 20 counts | `stereo_seq` |
| Slide-seq / Slide-seqV2 / Curio Seeker | `*.digital_expression.txt[.gz]` (genes × beads) + `*bead_locations.csv` / `BeadLocationsForR.csv` (`barcodes, xcoord, ycoord`), or `*MoleculesPerMatchedBead.mtx` + `barcodes.tsv` + `genes.tsv` + `*MatchedBeadLocation.csv` | bead coordinates as written | beads < 10 counts | `slide_seq` |
| Spatial Genomics seqFISH | `*CellxGene.csv` + `*CellCoordinates.csv` (`label, area, center_x, center_y`) | microns | cells < 10 counts | `seqfish` (= `merfish`) |
| generic counts + coordinates | `staig.io.read_table(counts, coordinates)`: CSV/TSV (cells × genes or genes × cells, orientation detected), MTX + barcodes/genes, 10x `.h5`; coordinates CSV/TSV with an id column and x/y columns (`x/y`, `X/Y`, `center_x/center_y`, `xcoord/ycoord`, `CenterX_global_px/...`); x/y columns inside the counts table also work | as written | `Blank*`, `NegPrb*` ... columns | by size (`auto`) |
| transcript lists | `staig.io.read_transcripts(path)`: Xenium `transcripts.parquet`, CosMx `tx_file.csv` (cells keyed `fov_cell_ID`), MERSCOPE `detected_transcripts.csv` with cell ids, STARmap/seqFISH molecule tables — aggregated to cells (position = count-weighted mean of the cell's transcripts; whole-slide coordinates preferred, per-FOV pixels rejected for several FOVs) | as written | unassigned transcripts, control genes (counted per cell); cells < 10 transcripts | by size |
| AnnData `.h5ad` | `obsm["spatial"]`, or x/y columns in `obs`; `X` is kept as stored (it may already be normalised; `staig run` detects that) | as stored | observations without finite coordinates | `auto` |

Every platform reader returns raw counts in `X` (CSR float32, negative values are rejected),
`obsm["spatial"]` as finite `(x, y)`, the platform's per-cell metadata in `obs`, `var["feature_types"]`
when the platform provides it, observation ids as the platform wrote them (strings, leading zeros kept),
and in `uns["staig"]`: `platform`, `source`, `coordinate_unit`, `qc` (`min_counts`, `n_removed` and a
`removed` breakdown: low counts, missing coordinates/metadata, off-tissue bins, background, unassigned
transcripts, unlabelled spots), `dropped_features` with `obs["control_counts"]` whenever control
features were removed, and platform details (`bin_size_um`, `microns_per_pixel`, the `experiment.xenium`
summary, GEM/GEF headers ...). `min_counts=0` disables only the count filter; `drop_controls=False`
(`drop_blanks=False` for MERSCOPE) keeps control features where a reader has them (Visium, Visium HD,
Xenium, CosMx, seqFISH, tables, transcripts). An input that ends up with no observation raises an error
naming the reasons instead of returning an empty object.

Coordinates are left in the platform's units: STAIG only uses nearest-neighbour relations, so the unit
never changes the result. Visium and Visium HD data also get the scanpy `uns["spatial"]` entry (scale
factors, hires/lowres images), so `staig.pl.spatial` and histology feature extraction work as for the
paper data.

## What `staig.run` does with each platform

* **Preprocessing** (`preprocess=True`): sequencing-based data (Visium, Visium HD, Stereo-seq,
  Slide-seq) get 3000 highly variable genes (`seurat_v3` on counts), normalisation to 10⁴, `log1p` and
  scaling — the pipeline of the paper. Targeted panels (Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMx, seqFISH, MERFISH,
  STARmap) use every gene. Matrices in which fewer genes vary than are requested skip the loess fit
  (all varying genes are used); when the `seurat_v3` loess fit fails on a very sparse matrix (common
  for Visium HD subsets), the fit is repeated on detected genes and, failing that, the log-based
  `seurat` flavour is used; `uns["staig"]["preprocess"]["hvg_note"]` records this. The same recovery is
  used when slices are concatenated. `preprocess=False` keeps an existing `obsm["X_staig_input"]`
  untouched, also for lists of inputs.
* **Preset** (`preset="auto"`): chosen from `uns["staig"]["platform"]` (table above) — image-guided
  edge removal and debiased negatives for Visium with histology features, fixed edge removal and no
  pseudo-labels otherwise; two GCN layers for high-resolution sequencing platforms.
* **Scale**: the exact contrastive denominator is used up to 65 536 observations on a GPU (8 000 on a
  CPU); above that `n_negatives="auto"` samples 8 192 (4 096 on CPU) negatives per step, so a whole
  Visium HD capture area at 8 µm (hundreds of thousands of bins) trains in bounded memory. Use 16 µm
  bins for a first look.
* **Histology**: for Visium folders (and `.h5ad` files) the full-resolution image found next to the
  data is used automatically (`image="auto"`); for every other platform `image="auto"` does nothing
  (the patch size of the paper is tied to the 55 µm spot). Pass `image=` and
  `image_kwargs={"patch_px": ...}` explicitly if you want to try histology on Visium HD. With several
  inputs an explicit `image=` is rejected: extract features per slice first and pass the AnnData objects.
* **Several inputs**: `staig.run([path_a, path_b])`, `staig run a/ b/` or `a;b` in the GUI read every
  input, name the slices after the folders (dict keys, or the run folder's name for `.../outs`), and
  concatenate them: every gene when all inputs are targeted panels, otherwise the genes among the
  5 000 most variable of every slice (the paper's integration setting). The integration preset is used
  with `batch_key="slice"` (or the key you pass). `uns["staig"]` records `platforms`, `sources` and
  `slices`; the merged `platform` is `"mixed"` when they differ.

## Validation on vendor sample files

The readers were developed against the official sample bundles below and the raw files shipped with the
paper's Zenodo dataset; `tests/test_io.py` replays the same layouts synthetically on every CI run and
`tests/test_io_samples.py` checks the real files when `STAIG_SAMPLES` points to a folder holding them.

| sample | software / source | read as | `staig run` (1 seed, RTX 5090) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Xenium_Prime_Mouse_Ileum_tiny` (10x) | Xenium Onboard Analysis 3.0, 23 cells, 5 006 genes | `xenium`: 11 cells after QC, 8 774 control features dropped | too few cells to cluster |
| `Visium_HD_Tiny_3prime_Dataset` (10x) | Space Ranger 4.0.1 | `visium_hd` 8 µm: 10 605 bins; 16 µm: 3 321; `level="cells"`: 612 segmented cells (mapping-derived positions; the GeoJSON fallback gives area centroids within 7 px of them) | 62 s, 3 domains; cells: 16 s, 9 domains |
| `CytAssist_FFPE_Protein_Expression_Human_Breast_Cancer` (10x) | Space Ranger 2.1, `tissue_positions.csv`, 35 Antibody Capture features | `visium`: 4 169 spots × 18 085 genes | 18 s, 3 domains |
| seqFISH v2 test data set (Spatial Genomics, via scverse) | `Roi1_CellxGene.csv`, `Roi1_CellCoordinates.csv` | `seqfish`: 58 cells × 12 genes | 5 s |
| CosMx HGSOC slide (Zenodo 8287971) | AtoMx flat files, 980 columns incl. 19 `NegPrb` | `cosmx`: 38 161 cells × 960 genes | 232 s, 3 domains |
| CosMx per-FOV exports (Zenodo 18602259) | two FOVs of different slides, `cell_ID == 0` background rows | `cosmx`: 2 054 and 3 352 cells × 968 genes | 12 s; both slides integrated: 24 s |
| Stereo-seq bin1 GEM (cartloader starter, Zenodo 17953582) | 18 M rows `geneID x y MIDCounts` | `stereo_seq` bin 50: 9 082 bins × 23 463 genes | 56 s, 4 domains |
| Stereo-seq cell-bin table (paper data, `Cell_GetExp_gene.txt`) | `geneID x y UMICount label` | `stereo_seq` cells: 19 247 cells × 27 106 genes | 104 s, 3 domains |
| STARmap transcript list (cartloader starter) | `X Y gene count cell_id Z` | `read_transcripts`: 14 816 cells × 1 022 genes | — |

The square-bin and cell-bin GEF readers follow the SAW file-format manual (software V7.1, document
A4.2: `geneExp/binN/expression` with `x, y, count`, `geneExp/binN/gene` with `gene, offset, count`;
`cellBin/cell`, `cellBin/cellExp`, `cellBin/gene`; the `offset` tables are honoured and validated) and
are tested on files written to that specification, including reversed offsets; a GEF from a SAW run
that behaves differently is a bug report we want. Slide-seq and Curio layouts follow the Broad / Curio
documentation and the STAGATE tutorial that loaded the paper's Slide-seqV2 data and are tested on
synthetic files only.

Download commands for the public samples:

```bash
curl -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/xenium/3.0.0/Xenium_Prime_Mouse_Ileum_tiny/Xenium_Prime_Mouse_Ileum_tiny_outs.zip
curl -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/spatial-exp/4.0.1/Visium_HD_Tiny_3prime_Dataset/Visium_HD_Tiny_3prime_Dataset_outs.zip
curl -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/spatial-exp/2.1.0/CytAssist_FFPE_Protein_Expression_Human_Breast_Cancer/CytAssist_FFPE_Protein_Expression_Human_Breast_Cancer_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5
curl -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/spatial-exp/2.1.0/CytAssist_FFPE_Protein_Expression_Human_Breast_Cancer/CytAssist_FFPE_Protein_Expression_Human_Breast_Cancer_spatial.tar.gz
curl -O https://s3.embl.de/spatialdata/raw_data/seqfish-2-test-dataset.zip
curl -O "https://zenodo.org/records/8287971/files/Run5452_S2_exprMat_file.csv?download=1"   # + metadata_file, fov_positions_file
curl -O "https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/stereoseq_starter.raw.tar.gz?download=1"
```

## Notes and limits

* `.parquet` files (Visium HD positions, Xenium tables) need `pyarrow`: `pip install "staig[io]"`.
  Xenium falls back to `cells.csv.gz` when pyarrow is missing.
* `staig inspect` shows the detection and the QC summary without training; in Python
  `staig.io.detect_platform` returns the platform name (it reads nothing) and `staig.io.summary(adata)`
  prints the QC summary. An unrecognised folder raises an error listing its files and the supported
  layouts, and a folder that matches several layouts asks for `platform=`; use `read_table` for anything
  else.
* The silhouette-based choice of the number of domains is a heuristic (it tends to pick few domains on
  large single-cell data sets); pass `n_clusters` when you know the number of domains.
* Negative-control counts are kept per cell in `obs["control_counts"]` for QC.
* MERSCOPE `detected_transcripts.csv` can only be aggregated when it carries a cell-id column (newer
  Vizgen post-processing); otherwise use the `cell_by_gene.csv` export.
* Memory: GEM and transcript tables are aggregated in 4-million-row chunks and dense tables are
  converted to sparse in row blocks; a whole 18-million-row Stereo-seq GEM still needs a few GB of RAM
  while it is read, and training keeps a dense `N × genes` input matrix (3 000 columns after HVG
  selection, every gene for panels).
* Stereo-seq bins are anchored at multiples of the bin size in chip coordinates (stereopy anchors at
  the smallest observed coordinate instead), so the same bin grid is obtained whatever the tissue
  region; header offsets are recorded, not applied.
* CosMx per-FOV pixel coordinates (`coordinates="local"`, `x_local_px`) overlap between FOVs and are
  only meaningful for one FOV.


---

<!-- Source: docs/tutorials/custom_image_features.md -->

# Bring your own image features

Any model can supply one feature vector per retained spot. The image API
accepts a NumPy array or a **string** ending in `.npy` through `method=`. It
does not invoke the external encoder or infer barcode alignment.

## Runnable example with released features

```python
import os
import numpy as np
import staig
from staig import datasets, img, metrics

adata = datasets.load_dlpfc("151673", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True)
features = np.asarray(adata.obsm.pop("image_features"), dtype=np.float32)
assert features.ndim == 2 and features.shape[0] == adata.n_obs
assert np.isfinite(features).all()
img.extract_image_features(adata, method=features)
model = staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, epochs=10, device="cpu", verbose=False)
print(metrics.evaluate(adata))
```

Replace `features` with the output of your chosen pathology model. Use its
documented preprocessing, patch resolution and licensing conditions. Store
barcodes alongside feature rows and reindex them to `adata.obs_names` after
filtering; matching the row count alone cannot detect shuffled rows. Feature
width is flexible and is not restricted to ResNet-50's 2048 dimensions.

Assigning `adata.obsm["image_features"] = features` directly is also supported.
The API route additionally records `uns["staig"]["image"]["method"]` as
`"precomputed"`. It stores float32 raw features; model preparation standardises
and projects them through PCA. The `[image]` extra is not required merely to
attach an existing array and train the graph model.

## Replacing features after a previous run

Prefer a freshly loaded AnnData. If you replace features on a trained object,
clear the derived image PCs, pseudo-labels and edge probabilities before
retraining; otherwise preparation may reuse them. The following continues the
example above, retaining the same input array only to demonstrate invalidation:

```python
adata.obsm["image_features"] = features.copy()
adata.obsm.pop("image_pcs", None)
adata.obs.drop(columns=["staig_pseudo_label"], errors="ignore", inplace=True)
adata.obsp.pop("staig_edge_prob", None)
model = staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, epochs=10, device="cpu", verbose=False)
```

Changing coordinates or the spot set also requires rebuilding the spatial graph.
The [executed custom-feature notebook](../examples/04_custom_image_features.ipynb)
extracts simple RGB patch statistics from real H&E data and passes them as an
array. Those descriptors demonstrate the interface; they are not a pretrained
foundation model or the published BYOL representation.


---

<!-- Source: docs/tutorials/integration.md -->

# Alignment-free integration of tissue slices

Use a separate AnnData object per slice. Coordinates remain in each slice's
native system; `batch_key` makes the spatial graph block-diagonal. Integration
learns a shared latent representation rather than registering tissue images.

```python
import os
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import staig
from staig import datasets, pp, metrics, pl

slice_ids = ["151675", "151676"]
slices = [datasets.load_dlpfc(s, root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True)
          for s in slice_ids]
merged = pp.concat_slices(
    slices, batch_key="slice", batch_categories=slice_ids, n_top_genes=5000,
)
model = staig.run(
    merged, n_clusters=7, preset="integration", batch_key="slice",
    preprocess=False, refine=False, epochs=10,
    device="cpu", loss_chunk_size=256, seed=0, verbose=False,
)
pl.spatial(merged, color="staig_domain", batch_key="slice")
plt.show()
print(metrics.evaluate(merged, batch_key="slice"))
```

`concat_slices` copies the inputs, selects HVGs per slice and uses their
intersection as `X_staig_input`. Its default normalisation is appropriate for
raw counts and its default `scale=False` follows the integration workflow. For
pre-normalised slices, pass `normalize=False, log1p=False, flavor="seurat"`.
Do not concatenate already preprocessed count slices and normalise again.

Raw image features are carried over when present in every input. Model
preparation computes image PCs per slice and uses image-based edge removal;
without images, the integration preset uses gene-based edge removal. For
image-free integration, load slices with `image_features=None`. The preset
disables pseudo-label debiasing and restricts negatives to the same slice.

Integration defaults to `refine=False`, matching the example. If refinement is
required, `run(..., refine=True, batch_key="slice")` now forwards the batch key
to its final refinement step. You can also call
`staig.cluster.refine_labels(merged, batch_key="slice")` explicitly. Neighbours
are selected separately within each slice. The plotting wrapper similarly draws
separate coordinate panels; concatenation does not preserve per-slice H&E
display metadata.

## Check mixing and biological structure together

`metrics.evaluate(..., batch_key="slice")` writes the returned metrics under
`merged.uns["staig"]["metrics"]`. BatchKL is a Python implementation: lower
values indicate neighbourhood batch proportions closer to the overall mixture.
iLISI (pure-Python port of the LISI algorithm) reports the median effective batch diversity: higher
values indicate more mixing. Neither metric proves that distinct biological
domains were preserved. Inspect ARI/NMI where annotations exist and spatial
maps of each slice alongside mixing scores.

The [executed notebook](../examples/03_integration_dlpfc_two_slices.ipynb)
also checks that no spatial edge crosses slice boundaries. Its ten-epoch CPU
run demonstrates the workflow of [paper Figure 5a](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-56276-0/figures/5);
use `preset="paper_integration_vertical"` with its full epoch count for the experiment itself.


---

<!-- Source: docs/tutorials/large_datasets.md -->

# Large datasets and memory

STAIG trains on the full graph. Sparse spatial edges and chunked contrastive
loss reduce peak memory. Exact loss compares every anchor with all spots and
retains quadratic total work; sampled negatives approximate its denominator.
Neither mode is mini-batch GNN training.

## Estimate the working set

The following standalone calculation estimates individual arrays, not peak
process memory:

```python
n_spots, n_genes, chunk = 20_000, 3_000, 256
gib = 1024 ** 3
print("float32 expression input, GiB:", n_spots * n_genes * 4 / gib)
print("one loss block, GiB:", chunk * n_spots * 4 / gib)
print("one uint8 patch cache, GiB:", n_spots * 512 * 512 * 3 / gib)
```

Several loss blocks, masks, gradients and model states coexist. Preprocessing
materialises a dense `N × F` feature matrix in host RAM even when `adata.X` is
sparse. Float64 roughly doubles array storage. Lower `loss_chunk_size` reduces
temporary device memory at the cost of more chunk/recomputation overhead;
reduce `n_top_genes` before training if expression storage is the bottleneck.

For an executable full-data example with conservative CPU settings, see
[Stereo-seq](no_histology.md). A GPU run can use the same API with `device="cuda"`;
measure free GPU memory before choosing a chunk size. CPU execution avoids GPU
pressure but still needs host RAM and can take much longer.

## Sampled negatives with `n_negatives`

`n_negatives="auto"` is the current default: training uses 4,096 sampled nodes
on CPU when there are more than 8,000 spots, and exact negatives otherwise
(including CUDA and MPS). These thresholds are implementation settings, not
measured hardware limits. Use `n_negatives=None` or `0` for exact loss, or an
integer `K` smaller than the number of spots to request sampled negatives.
A value at least as large as the dataset also selects exact loss.

The sampled path keeps graph positives exact and estimates the denominator from
a random subset shared across anchors, rescaled by `N / K`. Its main similarity
blocks have shape `loss_chunk_size × K` rather than `loss_chunk_size × N`.
This is an approximation that can change the fitted result; do not label it a
numerically identical paper reproduction. Record the resolved value in
`adata.uns["staig"]["n_negatives"]` (`"all"` for exact) with the configuration.
The [Stereo-seq example](no_histology.md) explicitly sets `n_negatives=4096`.

## Image caches and other memory costs

`img.extract_image_features(..., cache_dir=...)` writes `patches.npy` and, when
filtering, `patches_filtered.npy` as uint8 memory maps. Each holds
`N × patch_size × patch_size × 3` bytes plus a small header; budget for both.
At 20,000 spots and 512 pixels, that is about 14.65 GiB per cache, a calculated
storage estimate. The full-resolution image itself is loaded into RAM in this
revision. Use `n_jobs=1` to limit filter-worker copies and `num_workers=0` to
limit image-loader workers. BYOL `batch_size` controls training; internal
embedding inference still uses batches of 128 in this revision.

Filtered caches are reused based only on row count. Use a separate cache for
every image, ordered barcode set and crop/filter configuration. Changing
`patch_size` also requires a matching frequency `band` centred on the new FFT
grid; leaving `(245, 275)` on a smaller patch is incorrect. Reusing released
features skips patch storage entirely.

Clustering and scoring can be more expensive than graph storage. Ward
initialisation in default GMM clustering can require quadratic memory; use
`cluster_method="kmeans"` when appropriate. Full silhouette evaluation also
performs pairwise-distance work. Consensus builds a dense co-association matrix
up to its `max_dense` threshold; lower that threshold to use the membership
representation path on large inputs. None of these choices is an automatic
guarantee of fitting a given CPU or GPU.


---

<!-- Source: docs/tutorials/no_histology.md -->

# Data without histology

Expression and `obsm["spatial"]` are sufficient. `run` defaults to
`preset="auto"`, which selects a configuration from the batch key, image/Visium
metadata and gene count. Choose the platform preset explicitly when you know
the assay; this heuristic does not identify every platform uniquely.

| Platform | Preset | Example archive member under `other/` | Expression state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stereo-seq | `stereo_seq` | `Mouse_Olfactory_Stereo-seq/filtered_feature_bc_matrix_norm.h5ad` | Already normalised |
| Slide-seqV2 | `slide_seq` | `Mouse_Olfactory_slide-seqV2/v2.h5ad` | Already normalised |
| STARmap | `starmap` | `starmap/starmap_norm.h5ad` | Already normalised |
| MERFISH | `merfish` | `Merfish/mouse1.AUD_TEA_VIS.242.unexpand_cluster3.h5ad` | Counts in this release |

These presets use fixed edge removal without image pseudo-label debiasing.
Stereo-seq, Slide-seq and STARmap presets use two graph layers; MERFISH uses one.
Inspect your own h5ad's provenance rather than inferring normalisation from the
platform name. The archive also contains count-based Slide-seq files.

## Stereo-seq example

```python
import os
import staig
from staig import datasets, pp, pl, metrics

adata = datasets.load_h5ad(
    "Mouse_Olfactory_Stereo-seq/filtered_feature_bc_matrix_norm.h5ad",
    root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True,
)
adata.var_names_make_unique()
if "spatial" not in adata.obsm:
    columns = ["X", "Y"] if {"X", "Y"} <= set(adata.obs) else ["x", "y"]
    adata.obsm["spatial"] = adata.obs[columns].to_numpy()

pp.preprocess(
    adata, n_top_genes=3000, normalize=False, log1p=False,
    flavor="seurat", scale=False,
)
model = staig.run(
    adata, n_clusters=7, preset="stereo_seq", preprocess=False,
    epochs=5, device="cpu", loss_chunk_size=256, n_negatives=4096, image=None,
    cluster_method="kmeans", refine=False, verbose=False,
)
pl.spatial(adata, color="staig_domain", img_key=None)
print(metrics.evaluate(adata, label_key=None))
```

The small epoch count, sampled negatives and k-means make this an execution
example, not a paper reproduction. `image=None` disables automatic image
extraction. The [notebook](../examples/02_no_histology_stereo_seq.ipynb)
records its full-data run and finite-loss checks.

For log-normalised inputs, `normalize=False, log1p=False` prevents a second
transformation; `flavor="seurat"` selects HVGs in that space. The paper's own
processing applied `seurat_v3` to these files, which `strict_counts=False`
reproduces.

For raw-count inputs, use `pp.preprocess(adata)` before `run(...,
preprocess=False)`, or let `run` preprocess automatically. For the example
MERFISH files, annotations may be named `cluster_L2`; pass
`label_key="cluster_L2"` to `metrics.evaluate` when using those labels. Without
annotations, SC and DB describe embedding structure, not anatomical truth.
Choose a domain count for your scientific question; automatic cluster-number
selection is available by omitting `n_clusters` but can be expensive.


---

<!-- Source: docs/tutorials/reproducing_the_paper.md -->

# Running the settings of the paper

The experiments of [Yang *et al.* (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56276-0) are available as
presets and scripts. The `paper_*` presets carry the per-dataset settings of the paper (float64, the
seeds, τ, epochs, image pseudo-labels, image PCs and the loss convention of version 1); the curated
datasets, including the released histology features, come from
[Zenodo record 14231773](https://zenodo.org/records/14231773).

## Presets

```python
import staig

for name in sorted(staig.PRESETS):
    if name.startswith("paper_"):
        print(name, staig.preset_config(name).to_dict())
```

| preset | experiment |
|---|---|
| `paper_151673` | DLPFC slice 151673 with histology (Figure 2) |
| `paper_integration_vertical` | adjacent DLPFC slices 151675 + 151676 (Figure 5a) |
| `paper_integration_horizontal` | mouse brain anterior + posterior (Figure 5b) |
| `paper_mouse_olfactory_stereo` | Stereo-seq mouse olfactory bulb (Figure 4) |
| `paper_slideseq_olfactory` | Slide-seqV2 mouse olfactory bulb (Figure 4) |
| `paper_starmap` | STARmap mouse visual cortex (Figure 4) |
| `paper_merfish` | MERFISH mouse visual cortex (Figure 4) |

## A DLPFC slice with histology

```python
import os
import staig
from staig import datasets, metrics, pl

adata = datasets.load_dlpfc("151673", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True)   # counts, labels, features
model = staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, preset="paper_151673", n_seeds=1, smooth=False, image=None)
print(metrics.evaluate(adata))            # ARI / NMI against the layer annotation
pl.spatial(adata, color=["ground_truth", "staig_domain"])
```

`image=None` keeps the released histology features of the slice (`obsm["image_features"]`) instead of
extracting new ones; drop it to recompute them from the full-resolution image. `n_seeds=1` and
`smooth=False` run the single training of the paper; the version 2 defaults (`n_seeds=3` on a GPU,
`smooth=True`) add the consensus and smoothing steps on top of it.

## The command-line scripts

`benchmarks/run_dlpfc.py` runs any configuration on one or all annotated DLPFC slices and writes a
per-seed CSV (ARI/NMI before and after refinement, training time):

```bash
python benchmarks/run_dlpfc.py --root "$STAIG_DATA" --slices 151673 --preset paper_151673 \
  --seeds 39788 --cluster gmm --tag paper
python benchmarks/run_dlpfc.py --root "$STAIG_DATA" --slices all \
  --paper-configs configs/paper/train_img_config.yaml --seeds paper --tag paper_all
```

`--paper-configs` replays the per-slice YAML settings shipped with version 1 (`configs/paper/`);
`--seeds 0,1,2` runs several seeds; `--features-dir` reads replacement image features named
`<slice>.npy`; `--cluster mclust` uses R mclust through the optional `[r]` extra.
`benchmarks/run_no_image.py` covers the Stereo-seq, Slide-seqV2, STARmap and MERFISH experiments and
`benchmarks/run_integration.py` the integration scenarios (`dlpfc_7576`, `dlpfc_4`, `mouse_brain`,
`merfish_vis`, `cross_platform`), with BatchKL and iLISI.

## Reporting

Run several seeds (`--seeds 0,1,2` or `run(n_seeds=...)`) and report the distribution; record the
preset, overrides, package versions, device and dtype with the result. The consensus labelling of
`run(n_seeds=...)` is a stable summary of the seeds; `uns["staig"]["consensus"]` records the seeds and
their agreement with the consensus.


---

<!-- Source: docs/tutorials/visium_with_histology.md -->

# Visium with histology

The [quick start](../quickstart.md) uses released H&E features. The
[executed notebook](../examples/01_visium_dlpfc_with_histology.ipynb) uses the full
labelled slice, short CPU training and these same released features. Fresh BYOL
extraction below is a separate, more expensive workflow.

## Load expression and spatial metadata

```python
import os
import staig
from staig import datasets, img, metrics, pl

adata = datasets.load_dlpfc(
    "151673", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True, image_features=None,
)
assert adata.obsm["spatial"].shape == (adata.n_obs, 2)
assert adata.obs_names.is_unique
```

For your own Space Ranger output, use `datasets.load_visium_dir` with the folder
containing `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` and `spatial/`. Label and feature files
are optional. The extractor expects full-resolution `(x, y)` coordinates, where
`x` is column and `y` is row, in exactly `adata.obs_names` order. A display image
such as `tissue_hires_image.png` has a different scale and should not replace
the full-resolution image without transforming coordinates and patch dimensions.

## Crop, filter and learn image features

```python
img.extract_image_features(
    adata,
    method="byol",
    epochs=1,
    batch_size=16,
    num_workers=0,
    n_jobs=1,
    cache_dir=".cache/151673-byol-default",
)
assert adata.obsm["image_features"].shape == (adata.n_obs, 2048)
```

The default patch width is `3.5 * fiducial_diameter_fullres`, then resized to
512 pixels per side. The filter uses the frequency window `(245, 275)` on those
patches. These are the settings of the paper (see
[DESIGN.md](https://github.com/y-itao/STAIG/blob/main/docs/dev/DESIGN.md)). Supply
`image=` and `patch_px=` when automatic image lookup or fiducial metadata is
unavailable. Edge patches are zero-padded with a warning.

Use a new cache directory whenever the image, barcode order, patch size, crop
scale or filtering settings change. Existing filtered patches are checked only
for row count, so an equal-length but differently ordered cache is not safe.
Keep BYOL batch sizes at least two and avoid a final singleton batch because
its projector uses batch normalisation. The published slice used here has no
singleton batch with the shown batch size.

`method="resnet50"` skips BYOL training and uses ImageNet features; it is a
different method. In this revision its inference batch is fixed internally at
128; the public `batch_size` argument controls BYOL training. Reusing
`embeddings.npy` through `method=<array>` avoids both extraction and weight
downloads and is the appropriate starting point for paper comparisons.

## Learn spatial domains and inspect them

```python
model = staig.run(
    adata, n_clusters=7, preset="visium", epochs=30,
    device="cpu", seed=0, verbose=False,
)
pl.spatial(adata, color=["ground_truth", "staig_domain"])
print(metrics.evaluate(adata))
pl.loss_curve(adata)
```

Thirty epochs are a workflow demonstration. Compare the loss curve, histology
and labels, and record the configuration before interpreting domain boundaries.
Newly extracted features can change clusters even with the same graph-model
seed. The [reproduction tutorial](reproducing_the_paper.md) separates these
choices from the published experiment.


---

<!-- Source: docs/faq.md -->

# Frequently asked questions

## How do I run the settings of the paper?

`preset="paper_151673"`, `"paper_integration_vertical"`, `"paper_integration_horizontal"`,
`"paper_mouse_olfactory_stereo"`, `"paper_starmap"`, `"paper_merfish"` and
`"paper_slideseq_olfactory"` replicate the per-dataset settings of the paper (float64, seeds, τ,
epochs, image PCs, pseudo-labels); `staig.datasets.load_dlpfc("151673", download=True)` gives the data
with the released histology features. The [reproduction page](tutorials/reproducing_the_paper.md)
lists the commands. Training is stochastic by design: seeds are fixed and recorded, `n_graph_samples`
resamples the augmented graphs, and `run(n_seeds=...)` returns a consensus labelling over several
seeds, which is the recommended way to obtain stable domains.

## Do I need scGeneClust, PyWGCNA, SpatialDE or R?

None is required for the v2 core pipeline. Python GMM is the default clusterer,
BatchKL and (i/c)LISI are implemented in pure Python (no R, no harmonypy). R plus rpy2 and
R's `mclust` are only needed if you explicitly choose `method="mclust"` (or
`cluster_method="mclust"` in `run`). Image extraction needs `[image]`;
Leiden needs `[cluster]` (Louvain additionally needs the `louvain` package, which has no wheels on some platforms). Follow [installation](installation.md) and
avoid mixing the v1 `requirements.txt` workflow with v2.

## Where are the datasets, and can I download only one slice?

Use [Zenodo record 14231773](https://zenodo.org/records/14231773). `STAIG_DATA`
points to the unpacked `Dataset` folder, not its parent. The downloader reads
the ZIP directory and selected members through HTTP Range requests:

```python
import os
from staig import datasets

datasets.download_dataset(
    root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), members=["DLPFC/151673"],
    include_full_image=False,
)
adata = datasets.load_dlpfc("151673", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"))
```

Omitting the full-resolution image keeps the released embeddings and smaller
display images; it prevents fresh full-resolution image extraction until that
TIFF is downloaded. Use `datasets.list_members()` to inspect exact member names.
Existing files of the expected size are skipped. New downloads are CRC-checked;
size-based resumption does not revalidate an existing file's CRC. Use
`overwrite=True` only when you intend to replace selected files. A loader's
`download=True` does not repair an already-existing incomplete slice folder.

## Where are the zebrafish melanoma data?

The original GEO samples are
[GSM4838131 (Visium-A)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM4838131)
and [GSM4838132 (Visium-B)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM4838132),
in [GSE159709](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE159709).
The curated Zenodo archive includes them under `v10x/`, in folders
`GSM4838131_Visium_A` and `GSM4838132_Visium_B`. The following loads one; availability
of labels, pretrained embeddings and full-resolution images varies by folder:

```python
import os
from staig import datasets

zebrafish = datasets.load_visium(
    "GSM4838131_Visium_A", root=os.getenv("STAIG_DATA"), download=True,
    labels=None, image_features=None,
)
```

See [paper Figure 7](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-56276-0/figures/7)
for the reported melanoma analysis.

## Can I use Visium HD, CosMx or another platform?

Yes, directly from the platform's output: `staig.run("path/to/outs")` or `staig run path/to/outs`
reads Space Ranger (Visium and Visium HD bins or segmented cells), Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMx/AtoMx
flat files, SAW `.gef`/`.gem` (Stereo-seq), Slide-seq / Curio Seeker, seqFISH and generic counts +
coordinates tables, removes control probes and empty cells and applies the platform's preprocessing.
`staig inspect path` shows what would be read. The layouts, defaults and the vendor sample files
each reader was validated on are listed in [Input formats](input_formats.md). Presets are starting
configurations. There is no end-to-end image pipeline for non-Visium images; supply
aligned external features through the [custom-feature API](tutorials/custom_image_features.md).
Large HD datasets need the [memory guidance](tutorials/large_datasets.md).

## Where does `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` come from?

It is a Space Ranger filtered feature/barcode count matrix supplied by the
original studies, not an output generated by STAIG. Original dataset sources
are listed in the paper's Supplementary Tables S1–S2 and
[data availability statement](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-56276-0#data-availability).
The accompanying `spatial/` files supply coordinates, image scaling and display
images. Keep the matrix and spatial files from the same sample together. A
pre-normalised h5ad is a different input and should not be renamed to this H5
filename.


---

<!-- Source: docs/agent_guide.md -->

# Using STAIG from an AI agent

STAIG learns spatial domains from expression, spatial neighbours and optional
histology, and integrates several slices without coordinate alignment. Install
from a checkout with `python -m pip install -e ".[image,cluster]"`; see
[installation](installation.md), the [API](api.md) and the
[AnnData keys contract](quickstart.md#anndata-keys). The public interfaces are
`staig.run`, `staig.pp`, `staig.img`, `staig.cluster` and `staig.metrics`.

## Decide whether STAIG fits

Input is an AnnData object with expression in `X` and finite coordinates in
`obsm["spatial"]`, or a Space Ranger Visium folder. Default preprocessing expects
raw counts. A full-resolution H&E image is optional; its pixel coordinates must
match the spots. Aligned precomputed image features can replace extraction.
For integration, each spot needs a slice identity in `obs[batch_key]`.

Outputs are categorical `obs["staig_domain"]`, embedding `obsm["X_staig"]`, sparse
graphs in `obsp`, and metadata in `uns["staig"]`. `staig.run` changes the input
AnnData **in place** and returns a fitted model. Save the AnnData to preserve
domains and embeddings; `model.save()` alone does not save those annotations.

Use STAIG for spatial domain exploration and comparing shared structure across
slices. It does not assign validated cell-type names, perform geometric image
registration, infer causal mechanisms, or establish clinical diagnoses. Without
spatial coordinates it is not the appropriate general scRNA-seq clustering tool.
Platform support means suitable expression/coordinate inputs can be used, not
that every bin size, panel, imaging modality or tissue has been validated.

## Platform outputs without an h5ad

`staig.read(path)` / `staig.run(path)` and `staig run path` accept Space Ranger (Visium, Visium HD),
Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMx, SAW (Stereo-seq), Slide-seq / Curio, seqFISH, generic counts + coordinates
tables, transcript lists and `.h5ad`; `staig inspect path` prints the detected platform and QC
summary. Reader options: `read_kwargs={"bin_size": 16}` (Visium HD µm / Stereo-seq DNBs),
`{"level": "cells"}` (Visium HD segmented cells), `{"min_counts": 0}`, `{"coordinates": "pos.csv"}`
(generic tables). Several paths = integration with `batch_key="slice"`. Details and the validated
sample files: [Input formats](input_formats.md).

## Four runnable recipes

Save each block as its own script after installing STAIG. Paths passed on the
command line are placeholders for your files. These examples use raw counts and
a known `n_clusters=7`; replace that value using biological context. Use fresh
AnnData: `run` reuses existing `X_staig_input`, graph and image-PC keys.

All four scripts print a JSON summary and write a new `.h5ad`. The longer
argparse versions in [`examples/`](https://github.com/y-itao/STAIG/tree/v2/examples)
accept `--input --n-clusters --output --preset --n-seeds --epochs`. They default
to CPU, reject overwriting an output, and offer `--log-normalized` for expression
already normalised and log-transformed. Their final stdout line is JSON; warnings
and progress can appear on stderr. Small `--epochs` values are smoke checks,
not paper-quality training.

### Visium plus H&E

Save as `visium_recipe.py`; run
`python visium_recipe.py spaceranger_out full_resolution_image.tif result.h5ad`.
This explicitly extracts BYOL features and may download ImageNet weights once.
The alternative `examples/run_visium.py` also accepts aligned released
`embeddings.npy`, avoiding fresh extraction.

```python
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import staig

started = time.perf_counter()
folder, image, output = sys.argv[1:]
if Path(output).exists():
    raise FileExistsError(output)
adata = staig.datasets.load_visium_dir(folder, image_features=None)
staig.img.extract_image_features(
    adata, image=image, device="cpu", num_workers=0, n_jobs=1,
)
staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, preset="visium", image=None, device="cpu")
scores = staig.metrics.evaluate(adata)
adata.write_h5ad(output)
print(json.dumps({"output_path": output, "metrics": scores,
                  "keys_written": ["obs/staig_domain", "obsm/X_staig", "uns/staig"],
                  "time_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}, allow_nan=False))
```

The Visium loader drops unlabelled spots when `truth.txt` exists, matching the
released embeddings. For your own data without that filtering, use `labels=None`
or `drop_na=False` and generate features for that exact barcode order.

### No image

Save as `no_image_recipe.py`; run `python no_image_recipe.py counts.h5ad result.h5ad`.
For already log-normalised data, replace `preprocess=True` with
`preprocess={"flavor": "seurat", "normalize": False, "log1p": False}`.

```python
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import scanpy as sc
import staig

started = time.perf_counter()
source, output = sys.argv[1:]
if Path(output).exists():
    raise FileExistsError(output)
adata = sc.read_h5ad(source)
for key in ("image_features", "image_pcs"):
    adata.obsm.pop(key, None)
staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, preset="auto", image=None, device="cpu", preprocess=True)
scores = staig.metrics.evaluate(adata)
adata.write_h5ad(output)
print(json.dumps({"output_path": output, "metrics": scores,
                  "keys_written": ["obs/staig_domain", "obsm/X_staig", "uns/staig"],
                  "time_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}, allow_nan=False))
```

`image=None` skips extraction; existing image features can still affect training.
That is why the no-image recipes remove both image feature keys on fresh input.

### Several slices

Save as `integration_recipe.py`; run
`python integration_recipe.py slice1.h5ad slice2.h5ad integrated.h5ad`.
All slices below contain raw counts. For log-normalised slices, pass
`flavor="seurat", normalize=False, log1p=False` to `concat_slices`.

```python
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import scanpy as sc
import staig

started = time.perf_counter()
*inputs, output = sys.argv[1:]
if Path(output).exists():
    raise FileExistsError(output)
slices = [sc.read_h5ad(path) for path in inputs]
adata = staig.pp.concat_slices(
    slices, batch_key="slice", batch_categories=[f"slice_{i}" for i in range(len(slices))],
)
staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, preset="integration", batch_key="slice",
          image=None, preprocess=False, refine=False, device="cpu")
scores = staig.metrics.evaluate(adata, batch_key="slice")
adata.write_h5ad(output)
print(json.dumps({"output_path": output, "metrics": scores,
                  "keys_written": ["obs/slice", "obs/staig_domain", "obsm/X_staig", "uns/staig"],
                  "time_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}, allow_nan=False))
```

`concat_slices` preprocesses each slice and uses the intersection of its HVGs.
The spatial graph stays block-diagonal; coordinates need not be aligned.
Images are not automatically extracted in batch mode. Extract per slice first
if wanted, with aligned `image_features` present on every input.

### Large data on CPU

Save as `large_recipe.py`; run `python large_recipe.py counts.h5ad result.h5ad`.
This uses approximate negative sampling, k-means and at most 2,000 spots for
evaluation. It avoids full-data silhouette selection by specifying the cluster
count. The same normalisation caveat as the no-image recipe applies.

```python
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import scanpy as sc
import staig

started = time.perf_counter()
source, output = sys.argv[1:]
if Path(output).exists():
    raise FileExistsError(output)
adata = sc.read_h5ad(source)
for key in ("image_features", "image_pcs"):
    adata.obsm.pop(key, None)
staig.run(adata, n_clusters=7, preset="auto", image=None, device="cpu",
          n_seeds=1, loss_chunk_size=256, n_negatives=1024,
          cluster_method="kmeans", refine=False)
idx = np.sort(np.random.default_rng(0).choice(adata.n_obs, min(2000, adata.n_obs), replace=False))
sample = adata[idx].copy()
scores = staig.metrics.evaluate(sample)
adata.uns["staig"]["metrics"] = scores
adata.uns["staig"]["metric_n_obs"] = sample.n_obs
adata.write_h5ad(output)
print(json.dumps({"output_path": output, "metrics": scores, "metric_n_obs": sample.n_obs,
                  "keys_written": ["obs/staig_domain", "obsm/X_staig", "uns/staig"],
                  "time_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}, allow_nan=False))
```

The model is still full-graph, with dense N-by-HVG input. Sampling negatives
changes the objective; it does not make every preprocessing/clustering step
constant-memory. See [large datasets](tutorials/large_datasets.md).

## Choosing n_clusters, preset and n_seeds

- **`n_clusters`:** use anatomical knowledge or an independent reference when
  available; seven is a DLPFC example, not a universal default. `None` searches
  3–15 clusters by silhouette in this revision. Inspect marker expression and
  spatial maps, and report the candidates tried. Large data should specify a
  count and compare candidates on a representative sample to limit cost.
- **`preset`:** `auto` chooses `integration` for multiple batches; otherwise
  Visium metadata/image features select `visium` or `visium_no_image`, <=1,500
  genes select `merfish`, and other inputs select `stereo_seq`. This is a
  heuristic. Explicit options include `slide_seq`, `starmap`, `merfish`,
  `stereo_seq`, `visium`, `visium_no_image` and `integration`. List all settings
  with `staig presets --show-default` or `staig.PRESETS`; resolve one with
  `staig.preset_config("visium").to_dict()`. `paper_*` presets replicate the per-dataset settings of
  the paper (float64, seeds, τ, epochs).
- **`n_seeds`:** the default `"auto"` means 3 (consensus) on a GPU and 1 on CPU; use 1 for a
  smoke run and 3–5 for consensus when resources permit. Training cost grows roughly with seed count,
  plus clustering/consensus. Up to 20,000 spots consensus materialises a dense
  N-by-N matrix temporarily; larger inputs use one-hot cluster memberships and
  k-means. Start with 1 for memory-constrained jobs. `X_staig` is the representative
  seed's embedding; the returned model/config/history/timings describe the last
  fitted seed, not all seeds or the total elapsed time. Record wall time yourself.

## Run times

Training time grows with the number of spots. A Visium section (3–5 k spots, 300 epochs) trains in
seconds on a GPU and in minutes on a laptop CPU; a 20 k-spot section takes a few minutes on a GPU;
above 65 536 observations on a GPU (8 000 on a CPU) the loss samples its negatives automatically and
the time grows linearly with the data. Histology feature extraction adds about a minute per Visium
section on a GPU (patch extraction and one BYOL epoch). Multi-seed consensus multiplies the training
time by `n_seeds`. Measure on the target machine before scheduling large jobs and record spot/gene
counts, preset, overrides, seeds, device, thread count and versions with the result.

## Validate the result

Run `staig.metrics.evaluate(adata)` after training: ARI/NMI are included only when
`obs["ground_truth"]` exists; `SC` (silhouette) and `DB` measure embedding separation
when more than one domain exists. For integration, supply `batch_key="slice"` to
add BatchKL and iLISI. These require the corresponding batch column and multiple
batches. Metric computation can be costly; the large-data recipe reports the
evaluation sample size explicitly.

Higher silhouette is better separation, not proof of anatomically correct
domains. Batch mixing can improve by erasing real biological differences, so
inspect tissue structure and marker expression per slice as well. Ensure
embeddings and losses are finite, labels cover all spots, and graphs have no
cross-slice edges. Compare independent seeds, unsmoothed and refined maps, and
any available held-out anatomical labels. Do not tune on the labels used to
claim final performance without disclosing that choice.

For marker review on a saved result whose `X` contains log-normalised expression:

```python
import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_h5ad("result.h5ad")
sc.tl.rank_genes_groups(adata, groupby="staig_domain", method="wilcoxon", use_raw=False)
sc.pl.rank_genes_groups(adata, n_genes=10)
```

Inspect known tissue markers and spatial maps too. Markers selected from the same
expression data that produced the domains are exploratory, not independent
validation. Keep raw counts separately when downstream analyses require them.

## Common errors and fixes

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Missing `obsm["spatial"]` | Load the spatial coordinate table and align rows by barcode. For Visium use full-resolution `(x, y)` pixels; do not substitute UMAP/PCA coordinates. |
| Non-integer counts warning / `strict_counts` | Check preprocessing history. `strict_counts=True` warns and switches from `seurat_v3` to `seurat`; it does not reject the input or prevent double normalisation. For already log-normalised expression use `preprocess={"flavor": "seurat", "normalize": False, "log1p": False}`. `strict_counts=False` forces the v1-style HVG calculation on non-integers; use only for deliberate historical compatibility. If raw counts are in a layer, pass `preprocess={"layer": "counts"}`. |
| No full-resolution image | Provide `image=".../full_resolution.tif"`, use aligned released/custom features, or run the no-image path. The low/hires images in `uns["spatial"]` are not automatic replacements for the full-resolution image. `image="auto"` skips extraction when none is discoverable. |
| CUDA out of memory | First lower `loss_chunk_size` (e.g. 256); the exact loss still uses chunk-by-N similarity work. Set `n_negatives=1024` for an approximate sampled objective, or use `device="cpu"`. Image extraction has its own `batch_size` and device controls via `image_kwargs`. `n_negatives="auto"` uses 4,096 sampled negatives only on CPU with >8,000 spots; otherwise it is exact. None, zero, or K>=N means exact. |
| Feature rows do not match spots | Generate/reindex features after barcode filtering; a matching row count alone does not prove alignment. |
| Stale results after parameter changes | `STAIG.prepare()` / `run()` recompute the graph, image PCs, edge probabilities and pseudo-labels whenever their parameters or the underlying coordinates, features or batch membership change (content fingerprints in `uns["staig"]`). `obsm["X_staig_input"]` is the one cached input: re-run `pp.preprocess` (or reload) when you change preprocessing, and avoid double preprocessing. |
| `.h5ad` save after automatic cluster selection | Works as is: `uns["staig"]["n_clusters_selection"]` uses string keys. The CLI refuses to overwrite an existing `--output` unless `--overwrite` is given. |

For tool-driven execution and the three tool schemas, see [MCP integration](mcp.md).
For the complete text bundle and discovery index, see [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt)
and [llms.txt](llms.txt). The index follows the [llms.txt convention](https://llmstxt.org/).


---

<!-- Source: docs/mcp.md -->

# STAIG MCP server

The optional local server exposes `staig_presets`, `staig_run` and
`staig_extract_image_features` over stdio using the
[MCP Python SDK's FastMCP API](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/tree/v1.x).
It reads local paths and creates local output files. It does not download
datasets; image extraction may download ImageNet weights on first use.

## Install and start

From a STAIG checkout, in your chosen Python environment:

```bash
python -m pip install -e ".[image,cluster,mcp]"
python -m staig.mcp_server
```

The last command waits for an MCP client on stdin; ordinary log output goes to
stderr. MCP is optional and is not imported by the base `staig` package.
FastMCP requires the SDK's 1.x line: an unbounded `mcp>=1.2` currently installs
2.x, where this API was renamed. The
[upstream 1.x documentation](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/blob/v1.x/README.md)
recommends a `<2` bound. This server was smoke-tested with `mcp==1.30.0`.

The package registers the following optional dependency and entry point in
`pyproject.toml`, so `staig-mcp` also starts the server after installation:

```toml
[project.scripts]
staig-mcp = "staig.mcp_server:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
mcp = ["mcp>=1.2,<2"]
```

Keep the `<2` bound when maintaining this FastMCP implementation. For older
checkouts without these packaging entries, install `mcp>=1.2,<2` separately and
use `python -m staig.mcp_server`.

## Claude Desktop and Claude Code

Merge this entry into `claude_desktop_config.json` (Desktop: Settings → Developer
→ Edit Config) or the project's `.mcp.json` for Claude Code. Replace the Python
path with the **absolute interpreter path** of the environment where STAIG and
MCP were installed; the Windows equivalent ends in `python.exe`. Do not replace
other servers in an existing file.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "staig": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/environment/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "staig.mcp_server"],
      "env": {
        "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": "",
        "OMP_NUM_THREADS": "4"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

This configuration selects CPU operation. CUDA use requires a suitable torch
build and removing the empty `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. You can also register the
stdio command with Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope project staig -- /absolute/path/to/environment/bin/python -m staig.mcp_server
```

Configuration references: [Claude Code MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)
and [connecting local servers to Claude Desktop](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers).
Registration is shown as documentation; this task did not modify a user's client
configuration or test an actual Claude Desktop/Code session.

## Tools

| Tool | Arguments | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `staig_presets()` | None | Mapping of preset names to complete resolved configurations. `auto` is a runtime selector, not a stored preset. |
| `staig_run(...)` | `input_path`, `n_clusters=None`, `preset="auto"`, `batch_key=None`, `n_seeds=1`, `output_path=None`, `platform="auto"`, `bin_size=None`, `min_counts=None` | Metrics, output path, spot/domain counts, core keys written, elapsed seconds |
| `staig_extract_image_features(...)` | `input_path`, `image_path`, `output_npy` | `.npy` path, feature shape/dtype, row-order description and elapsed seconds |

Example `staig_run` arguments:

```json
{
  "input_path": "/absolute/path/to/section.h5ad",
  "n_clusters": 7,
  "preset": "auto",
  "n_seeds": 1,
  "output_path": "/absolute/path/to/section_domains.h5ad"
}
```

`input_path` can be any platform output recognised by `staig.read` (Space Ranger, Visium HD,
Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMx, Stereo-seq, Slide-seq, seqFISH folders or files; see
[Input formats](input_formats.md)); `platform`, `bin_size` and `min_counts` are passed to the
reader. When `output_path` is omitted, the
output is a sibling `<input-stem>_staig.h5ad`. Existing paths, including the
input, are refused. `staig_run` uses the preset's full epoch count, automatic
image handling and standard refinement. It does not expose an epoch override;
use the [CLI examples](agent_guide.md#four-runnable-recipes) for a short pilot.

Input requirements and caveats:

- Expression defaults to raw counts. For already log-normalised `.h5ad`, first
  use `staig.pp.preprocess(adata, flavor="seurat", normalize=False, log1p=False)`
  and save the prepared `X_staig_input`. Do not rerun normalisation on that input.
- Several slices must already be concatenated (e.g. with `pp.concat_slices`) and
  saved, with `batch_key` identifying their non-missing slice labels. The tool
  accepts one path, not a list. Graphs must reflect that batch definition.
- Image extraction requires full-resolution coordinates and Visium
  `fiducial_diameter_fullres` metadata. Its output order matches the loaded
  `obs_names`; if `truth.txt` exists the Visium loader drops unlabelled spots.
  Load the same input with the same filtering before attaching the `.npy` via
  `staig.img.extract_image_features(adata, method="features.npy")`.
- The server performs real training, image extraction and evaluation. Large
  inputs, multi-seed consensus and full-data silhouettes can be expensive; the
  minimal server is intended for local bounded runs, not background scheduling.
  Choose client timeouts for the actual workload, or use the Python/CLI path.

## Tests

`tests/test_mcp_server.py` exercises the server with the SDK's in-memory client: tool discovery, a training
run through `staig_run` with its saved AnnData output, image extraction and the error responses.
